title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video and synthetic likeness tools were used to create a fake version of a real, named attorney. The fabricated videos were distributed across social media platforms at scale, with thousands of fake accounts created to reach targets. The failure did not originate inside a legitimate AI deployment but in the deliberate misuse of generative tools by outside actors who built a fraudulent service around a real person's identity.

The harm occurred at the point where potential clients encountered the fake content before any contact with the real attorney or any verifiable legal institution. At least one person is reported to have lost money after engaging with what they believed was a legitimate legal service. The scale of the operation, nearly 6,500 fake accounts removed across three platforms, indicates the content circulated for long enough that platform moderation alone did not catch it quickly.

What is not established is the identity of the scammers, whether any investigation has produced findings, or how many people suffered financial loss beyond the cases reported.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience says criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Angel Leal discovered that scammers created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring his likeness, offering immigration services he never provided. In one video, a digital version of Leal offered US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. Potential clients began calling his office after seeing these fraudulent videos on social media platforms.

The scam has escalated significantly over recent months, with an anti-piracy company helping remove nearly 6,500 fake accounts, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Scammers direct viewers to contact a WhatsApp number and send phony contracts, sometimes including fake testimonials from supposed former clients. Leal warns immigrants to be cautious of anyone requesting payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and to verify anyone offering legal services online. He plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud.
